# **1\. Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) describes the functional and non-functional requirements for the Kandypack Rail and Road-Based Supply Chain Distribution System, Version 1.0. This system is a database-driven logistics platform developed for Kandypack (Pvt) Ltd, a mid-sized FMCG manufacturing company located in Kandy, Sri Lanka.

The purpose of this document is to provide the development team, database administrators, project stakeholders, and testers with a complete, unambiguous description of what the system must do. It covers all entities, relationships, business rules, data constraints, stored procedures, triggers, and reporting requirements needed for Version 1.0 of the platform. This document replaces previous Excel-based tracking specifications and serves as the authoritative reference for system design and implementation.

## **1.2 Document Conventions**

This document follows the IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications. The following conventions apply throughout:

* All requirement identifiers follow the format REQ-XX-NNN where XX is the category code (FR \= Functional, NF \= Non-Functional, DB \= Database) and NNN is a three-digit sequence number.  
* Priority levels are assigned as HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW. All HIGH requirements must be satisfied before the first release.  
* Text in bold indicates a defined term found in Appendix A: Glossary.  
* The word "must" indicates a mandatory requirement. The word "should" indicates a recommended requirement. The word "may" indicates an optional requirement.

## **1.3 Intended Audience and Reading Suggestions**

This document is intended for the following audiences:

* Database Designers and Developers: Read all sections. Focus particularly on Sections 4 and 6, which contain detailed functional requirements, database schema notes, and procedure specifications.  
* Project Managers and Supervisors: Read Sections 1, 2, and 5\. These sections provide the project overview, scope, and non-functional quality requirements.  
* Testers and QA Personnel: Read Sections 4 and 5\. Pay special attention to the stimulus/response sequences and constraint requirements which define acceptance criteria.  
* End Users and Business Stakeholders: Read Sections 1.4, 2.1, and 2.2. These sections describe the system in non-technical terms.

## **1.4 Product Scope**

The Kandypack Rail and Road-Based Supply Chain Distribution System (hereafter referred to as "the System") is a database-driven logistics management platform designed to replace the company's existing Excel-based tracking processes.

Kandypack distributes finished FMCG goods from its Kandy factory to wholesale and retail customers in six major cities across Sri Lanka: Colombo, Negombo, Galle, Matara, Jaffna, and Trincomalee. Distribution is carried out in two stages. In the first stage, bulk goods are transported by Sri Lanka Railways from Kandy to the destination city. In the second stage, goods are stored at a city-based store near the railway station and then dispatched via road trucks on predefined routes for last-mile delivery to customer addresses.

The System will manage the complete lifecycle of an order: from placement through train trip scheduling, store unloading, truck route assignment, delivery, and final status update. It will also enforce all business rules automatically through database constraints, triggers, and stored procedures, and will produce six management reports. A basic user interface will be provided for key operations.

This SRS covers Version 1.0 only. Future versions may include mobile interfaces, integration with Sri Lanka Railways ticketing APIs, and real-time GPS tracking of trucks.

# **2\. Overall Description**

## **2.1 Product Perspective**

The System is a new, self-contained database platform. It does not replace any existing enterprise system but replaces a collection of Microsoft Excel spreadsheets currently used by Kandypack's logistics team. The System will be the single authoritative source of truth for all logistics data including orders, train bookings, store inventory, truck schedules, and delivery status.

The System interfaces with Sri Lanka Railways only at the business process level. There is no electronic integration with the railways in Version 1.0. Train schedules are entered manually by a system administrator. The System is self-hosted on a server at Kandypack's Kandy facility and accessed through a web browser by authorised staff.

***\[DIAGRAM: Figure 1 – System Context Diagram\]***

## **2.2 Product Functions**

The following is a high level summary of the major functions the System must perform :

* Order Management \- Accept customer orders with multiple product line items, validate the 7 day advance booking rule, match orders to delivery routes, and track order status through the full lifecycle.  
* Train Trip Scheduling \-  Maintain a schedule of train trips from Kandy to six cities, calculate cargo space consumed per order using product space rates, prevent overbooking, and handle overflow by scheduling excess cargo to the next available trip.  
* Store and Inventory Management \- Record goods received at city stores after train arrival, and track current stock levels at each store.  
* Truck and Route Management \-  Maintain predefined delivery routes with coverage areas and time limits, create and validate truck schedules, and enforce all driver/assistant roster rules automatically.  
* Delivery Tracking \-  Link deliveries to truck schedules, record delivery outcomes, and automatically update order status upon successful delivery.  
* Reporting \- Generate six management reports covering sales, product performance, driver hours, truck usage, and customer history.

*![][image2]*

***\[DIAGRAM: Figure 2 – High-Level Data Flow Diagram (Level 0)\]***

## **2.3 User Classes and Characteristics**

The System has five user classes :

| User Class | Description | Technical Level | Primary Functions Used |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Logistics Manager | Manages train schedules, oversees orders and routes | Intermediate | Train scheduling, order management, reports |
| Order Entry Clerk | Enters customer orders into the system | Basic | Place order, view order status |
| Store Manager | Receives goods at destination city stores | Basic | Receive goods, view inventory |
| Fleet Supervisor | Creates and manages truck delivery schedules | Intermediate | Truck scheduling, roster management |
| System Administrator | Manages master data: products, routes, staff | Advanced | All system functions, user management |

## **2.4 Operating Environment**

* Server \- Linux-based server hosted at Kandypack Kandy premises. Minimum 8GB RAM, 500GB storage.  
* Database \-  MySQL 8.0 or PostgreSQL 14 or later.  
* Application Layer \- Web application accessible via modern browsers (Chrome 110+, Firefox 110+, Edge 110+).  
* Client Devices \-  Desktop and laptop computers at Kandy head office and destination city stores. Internet connection required for store access.  
* Network \- Existing LAN at Kandy facility. Internet connectivity for remote store access.

## **2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints**

* The System must be implemented using a relational database management system (RDBMS) such as MySQL 8.0.  
* All business rules (capacity constraints, roster limits, 7 day advance order rule) must be enforced at the database level using triggers and constraints, not only in application code.  
* All multi step operations must be wrapped in transactions to ensure ACID compliance.  
* Foreign key constraints must be enabled and enforced for all relationships.  
* The system must support at least 40 orders, 10 delivery routes, and a valid train schedule with defined capacities as minimum test data.  
* The basic user interface must be a web-based application. Mobile interface is out of scope for Version 1.0.  
* No real time integration with Sri Lanka Railways systems is required. Train schedules are entered manually.

## **2.6 User Documentation**

* System Administration Manual \- Covers database setup, master data entry, user account management, and backup procedures.  
* User Operations Guide \-  Covers how to place orders, create truck schedules, receive goods, and run reports. Provided as a PDF document.  
* Quick Reference Cards \-  One-page laminated cards for Order Entry Clerks and Store Managers showing the most common tasks.

## **2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies**

* Train schedules are assumed to be fixed for each week and will be entered manually by the Logistics Manager at the start of each week.  
* Product space consumption rates are assumed as follows \- 1 box of detergent \= 0.5 space units , 1 bag of rice \= 1.0 space unit , 1 bottle of cooking oil \= 0.3 space units , 1 carton of biscuits \= 0.4 space units , 1 case of canned fish \= 0.6 space units , 1 carton of tea \= 0.2 space units. These rates are configurable in the database.  
* Standard train cargo capacity is assumed at 500 space units per trip. This is configurable per trip.  
* Train frequency is assumed as \- Galle, Matara – 2 trips per week ; Jaffna, Trincomalee, Negombo – 1 trip per week ; Colombo 3 trips per week;.  
* Truck delivery schedules operate between 06:00 and 20:00 only.  
* The working week is Monday to Saturday for drivers and assistants.  
* One unit of space is defined as the space occupied by one standard 50kg sack of rice.  
* The system depends on the availability of the MySQL database server. No automatic failover is included in Version 1.0.

# **3\. External Interface Requirements**

## **3.1 User Interfaces**

The system shall provide a web-based user interface with the following screens :

* Login Screen \- Username and password authentication with role-based access control.  
* Dashboard \-  Summary cards showing pending orders, today's train departures, active truck schedules, and low-stock alerts.  
* Place New Order \-  Form to select customer, add product line items with quantities, and choose expected delivery date. Real-time validation of the 7 day rule and route coverage.  
* View Orders \- Filterable and searchable list of all orders with status, customer name, city, and dates. Clicking an order shows full details.  
* Train Schedule Screen \- Calendar view of upcoming trips with current booked space and remaining capacity per trip. Allow adding new trips.  
* Truck Schedule Screen \- Create and view truck delivery schedules. Display conflict warnings if a driver, assistant, or truck is already booked. Show roster status.  
* Delivery Update Screen \- Mark deliveries as completed and record delivery notes.  
* Store Inventory Screen \- View current stock levels at each city store.  
* Reports Screen \- Run each of the six management reports with date range inputs, display results in a table, and allow export to CSV.

## **3.2 Hardware Interfaces**

The System does not interface directly with any hardware devices in Version 1.0. All data entry is through keyboard and mouse on standard desktop computers. Label printers and barcode scanners are out of scope for this version.

## **3.3 Software Interfaces**

* Database Management System: \- MySQL 8.0. The application layer connects to MySQL via JDBC or a standard connector library. Connection parameters (host, port, credentials) are stored in a configuration file.  
* Web Server \- Apache Tomcat 10 or Node.js 18+ serving the web application.  
* Browser \- Any modern browser supporting HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript ES6+.  
* No external API integrations are required for Version 1.0. Sri Lanka Railways schedule data is entered manually.

## **3.4 Communications Interfaces**

The system uses standard HTTP/HTTPS protocols. In Version 1.0, no email notifications, SMS alerts, or push notifications are required. All communication between users and the system is through the web interface. HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher must be used for all connections.

# **4\. System Features**

## **4.1 Order Management**

### **4.1.1 Description and Priority**

This feature covers the full order lifecycle from placement to delivery completion. It is the core feature of the system. Priority: HIGH.

### **4.1.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* Stimulus: Order Entry Clerk selects a customer and adds products with quantities. Response: System validates the delivery address against available routes and checks the 7-day advance rule.  
* Stimulus: Clerk submits the order. Response: System creates the order record, assigns a train trip, books cargo space, and sets status to "Pending".  
* Stimulus: Ordered quantity exceeds remaining train trip capacity. Response: System books the available space on the current trip and automatically schedules the remainder on the next available trip to the same city.  
* Stimulus: Manager views order list. Response: System displays all orders filterable by status, city, customer, and date range.

### **4.1.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-001:** The system must allow creation of an order for any registered customer. An order must contain at least one order item (product \+ quantity).

**REQ-FR-002:** The system must reject any order where the expected delivery date is fewer than 7 calendar days from the order placement date.

**REQ-FR-003:** The system must validate that the customer's delivery address falls within a covered delivery route before accepting an order.

**REQ-FR-004:** The system must automatically calculate total cargo space required for an order using the formula: Total Space \= SUM(quantity\_i × space\_rate\_i) for all order items i.

**REQ-FR-005:** The system must automatically assign the order to the nearest available train trip to the customer's destination city that has sufficient remaining capacity.

**REQ-FR-006:** If a train trip does not have sufficient capacity for the entire order, the system must split the order: book what space is available on the current trip, and schedule the remaining quantity on the next available trip to the same city.

**REQ-FR-007:** Each order must have a status that transitions through: Pending → In Transit → At Store → Out for Delivery → Delivered.

**REQ-FR-008:** The system must maintain a full audit trail of status changes with timestamps.

## **4.2 Train Trip Scheduling and Cargo Management**

### **4.2.1 Description and Priority**

This feature manages the allocation of cargo space on Sri Lanka Railways train trips from Kandy to six destination cities. It enforces capacity constraints and handles overflow. Priority: HIGH.

### **4.2.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* Stimulus: Admin enters a new train trip with destination and capacity. Response: System saves the trip and makes it available for order assignment.  
* Stimulus: Order is placed for a destination city. Response: System calls get\_available\_capacity() and assigns the order if space is sufficient.  
* Stimulus: Trip departs. Response: Logistics Manager updates trip status to "Departed". System updates all linked orders to "In Transit".  
* Stimulus: Trip arrives at destination. Response: Store Manager confirms goods receipt. System updates inventory and order status to "At Store".

### **4.2.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-010:** The system must maintain a train trip schedule with at minimum: trip ID, origin (always Kandy), destination city, departure date and time, arrival date and time, total cargo capacity (space units), and current booked space.

**REQ-FR-011:** The system must prevent any booking that would cause total booked space to exceed the trip's total cargo capacity. This must be enforced by a BEFORE INSERT trigger on the train\_bookings table.

**REQ-FR-012:** The system must provide a function get\_available\_capacity(trip\_id) that returns the remaining free space on a given trip as: total\_capacity \- total\_booked\_space.

**REQ-FR-013:** The system must provide a function get\_next\_available\_trip(city, after\_date) that returns the trip ID and departure date of the next scheduled trip to the given city after the specified date.

**REQ-FR-014:** The train schedule must support at minimum the following frequencies: Colombo 3 trips/week, Galle 2 trips/week, Matara 2 trips/week, Jaffna 1 trip/week, Trincomalee 1 trip/week, Negombo 1 trip/week.

*![][image4]*

***\[DIAGRAM: Figure 4 – State Transition Diagram: Train Trip\]***

## **4.3 Store Inventory Management**

### **4.3.1 Description and Priority**

This feature manages the receipt and storage of goods at destination city stores located near railway stations. Priority: HIGH.

### **4.3.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* Stimulus: Train arrives and goods are unloaded. Store Manager triggers "Receive Goods" for a trip. Response: System adds unloaded quantities to the store inventory for each product.  
* Stimulus: Store Manager views inventory. Response: System displays current stock of all products at that store.  
* Stimulus: Goods are loaded onto a delivery truck. Response: System deducts quantities from store inventory.

### **4.3.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-020:** Each destination city must have at least one store record linked to a railway station.

**REQ-FR-021:** The system must track inventory per product per store as a running total of available quantity.

**REQ-FR-022:** When goods are received from a train trip (procedure: receive\_goods\_at\_store), the system must increment inventory quantities for all products in that booking.

**REQ-FR-023:** When goods are dispatched on a truck delivery, inventory quantities must be decremented accordingly.

**REQ-FR-024:** The system must prevent dispatching more quantity than is currently in stock for any product at a store.

## **4.4 Truck Scheduling and Route Management**

### **4.4.1 Description and Priority**

This feature manages the assignment of delivery trucks to predefined routes with drivers and assistants, while enforcing all roster constraints. Priority: HIGH.

### **4.4.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* Stimulus: Fleet Supervisor creates a new truck schedule. Response: System validates no conflicts exist for the truck, driver, or assistant, checks roster rules, and creates the schedule.  
* Stimulus: Schedule creation violates a constraint. Response: System returns a specific error message identifying the conflicting resource and the violated rule.  
* Stimulus: Supervisor views available drivers for a time slot. Response: System displays all drivers who are free during that slot and within weekly hour limits.

### **4.4.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-030:** The system must maintain at least 10 predefined delivery routes. Each route must have: route ID, name, origin store, coverage area description, list of delivery zones/addresses served, and maximum delivery time in hours.

**REQ-FR-031:** Each truck schedule must assign exactly one truck, one driver, and one driver assistant. All three must be unique and conflict-free for the time slot.

**REQ-FR-032:** The system must prevent assigning the same truck to two overlapping time slots. This must be enforced by a BEFORE INSERT trigger on the truck\_schedules table.

**REQ-FR-033:** The system must prevent assigning the same driver to two overlapping time slots.

**REQ-FR-034:** The system must prevent assigning the same driver assistant to two overlapping time slots.

**REQ-FR-035:** A driver must not be scheduled for two consecutive truck deliveries (i.e., no back-to-back routes without a break in between). A "consecutive delivery" is defined as a second schedule whose start time is within 2 hours of the end of the immediately preceding schedule for the same driver.

**REQ-FR-036:** A driver assistant may be assigned to a maximum of two consecutive routes. On the third consecutive assignment, the system must reject the schedule.

**REQ-FR-037:** The total scheduled hours for any driver must not exceed 40 hours per calendar week (Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59).

**REQ-FR-038:** The total scheduled hours for any driver assistant must not exceed 60 hours per calendar week.

**REQ-FR-039:** The procedure schedule\_truck\_delivery must validate all constraints in REQ-FR-031 through REQ-FR-038 within a single transaction before inserting the schedule record.

***\[DIAGRAM: Figure 5 – Use Case Diagram: Truck Scheduling\]***

## **4.5 Delivery Tracking and Completion**

### **4.5.1 Description and Priority**

This feature tracks the last-mile delivery of orders from store to customer and updates order status upon completion. Priority: HIGH.

### **4.5.2 Stimulus/Response Sequences**

* Stimulus: Driver completes a delivery and the supervisor marks it as delivered. Response: System updates the delivery record status to "Completed" and automatically updates the linked order status to "Delivered" via a trigger.  
* Stimulus: Manager views customer order history. Response: System returns full order history including delivery details, driver name, truck ID, and completion time.

### **4.5.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-040:** Each delivery record must link a specific order to a specific truck schedule.

**REQ-FR-041:** A delivery record must have a status field: Scheduled, In Progress, or Completed.

**REQ-FR-042:** When a delivery status is updated to "Completed", an AFTER UPDATE trigger must automatically set the linked order's status to "Delivered" and record the delivery completion timestamp.

**REQ-FR-043:** The system must record delivery notes and any exceptions (e.g., partial delivery, customer not available) on the delivery record.

## **4.6 Management Reporting**

### **4.6.1 Description and Priority**

The system must produce six management reports. These reports query the live database and should return results within acceptable response times. Priority: HIGH for reports 1–3, MEDIUM for reports 4–6.

### **4.6.2 Report Specifications**

| Report \# | Report Name | Key Grouping | Output Fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Quarterly Sales Report | Quarter, Year | Total order value (LKR), total volume (units), number of orders |
| 2 | Most Ordered Items | Quarter, Product | Product name, total quantity, total value, rank |
| 3 | City-wise and Route-wise Sales | City, Route | City, route name, total orders, total value |
| 4 | Driver and Assistant Hours | Person, Week | Name, role, week start date, total hours, remaining hours |
| 5 | Truck Usage Analysis | Truck, Month | Truck ID, month, number of trips, total hours used |
| 6 | Customer Order History | Customer | Order ID, date, products, quantities, delivery date, driver, status |

### **4.6.3 Functional Requirements**

**REQ-FR-050:** Report 1 must aggregate total order value (sum of quantity × unit\_price for all delivered orders) and total volume (sum of quantities) grouped by quarter and year.

**REQ-FR-051:** Report 2 must rank products by total ordered quantity within a user-specified quarter and year.

**REQ-FR-052:** Report 3 must show total sales broken down first by destination city and then by delivery route within each city.

**REQ-FR-053:** Report 4 must calculate total scheduled hours for each driver and assistant in a specified week and compare against their respective limits (40 and 60 hours).

**REQ-FR-054:** Report 5 must show, per truck per month, the number of delivery runs completed and total hours the truck was in service.

**REQ-FR-055:** Report 6 must display the complete delivery history for a specified customer including product names, quantities, delivery date, driver name, and final delivery status.

# **5\. Non-Functional Requirements**

## **5.1 Performance Requirements**

**REQ-NF-001:** Order placement transactions (including train capacity check and booking) must complete within 3 seconds under normal load (up to 20 concurrent users).

**REQ-NF-002:** Truck schedule creation with full constraint validation must complete within 2 seconds.

**REQ-NF-003:** All six management reports must return results within 10 seconds when executed against a database containing up to 10,000 orders.

**REQ-NF-004:** The system must support at least 20 concurrent users without degradation in response time.

## **5.2 Safety Requirements**

**REQ-NF-005:** The system must perform automated daily backups of the database. Backup files must be stored in a location separate from the primary server.

**REQ-NF-006:** All transactions must be atomic. A failure at any step in a multi-step operation (e.g., place order \+ book train space) must roll back all changes made in that transaction.

**REQ-NF-007:** Triggers that enforce business rules must raise meaningful error messages that identify the specific rule that was violated (e.g., "Driver \[name\] would exceed the 40-hour weekly limit").

## **5.3 Security Requirements**

**REQ-NF-008:** All user accounts must be authenticated with a username and password. Passwords must be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt or equivalent).

**REQ-NF-009:** The system must implement role-based access control. Each user class (Section 2.3) must only have access to the screens and operations relevant to their role.

**REQ-NF-010:** All web traffic must be served over HTTPS using TLS 1.2 or higher.

**REQ-NF-011:** Database access credentials must not be hardcoded in application source code. They must be read from environment variables or a secured configuration file.

**REQ-NF-012:** All user actions that modify data (create, update, delete) must be logged with the user ID, timestamp, action type, and affected record ID.

## **5.4 Software Quality Attributes**

* Reliability: The system must achieve 99% uptime during business hours (06:00 – 22:00, Monday–Saturday). Planned maintenance windows must be scheduled outside business hours.  
* Maintainability: All stored procedures, functions, and triggers must be documented with inline comments. The database schema must include a data dictionary. Any business rule change must require no more than one trigger or procedure modification.  
* Portability: The database schema and all SQL code must be compatible with both MySQL 8.0 and PostgreSQL 14 to avoid vendor lock-in. Version 1.0 targets MySQL 8.0.  
* Usability: The web interface must be learnable by a new staff member with basic computer literacy within one hour of guided training. All forms must include inline validation messages.  
* Scalability: The database design must accommodate growth to 100,000 orders per year without architectural changes. Indexing strategy must be designed with this scale in mind.

## **5.5 Business Rules**

* **BR-001**: An order must be placed at least 7 calendar days before the expected delivery date.  
* **BR-002**: An order's delivery address must fall within a covered delivery route. Orders cannot be placed for addresses outside all defined routes.  
* **BR-003**: Each product consumes a defined amount of train cargo space. The total space consumed by all bookings on a trip must not exceed that trip's capacity.  
* **BR-004**: A driver must not be assigned to two consecutive truck deliveries without a break of at least 2 hours between them.  
* **BR-005**: A driver assistant may be assigned to at most two consecutive routes. The third consecutive route assignment must be refused.  
* **BR-006**: A driver must not exceed 40 scheduled hours in any calendar week.  
* **BR-007**: A driver assistant must not exceed 60 scheduled hours in any calendar week.  
* **BR-008**: A truck, driver, or assistant cannot be assigned to two overlapping time slots simultaneously.  
* **BR-009**: Quarterly sales reports must be calculated only from orders with status "Delivered".

# **6\. Other Requirements**

## **6.1 Database Requirements**

The following database-level requirements apply in addition to the functional requirements above:

* All tables must have a primary key. Surrogate integer primary keys (AUTO\_INCREMENT) are preferred.  
* Foreign key constraints must be defined for all relationships with appropriate ON DELETE and ON UPDATE actions.  
* The following indexes must be created as a minimum: orders(customer\_id), orders(status), orders(expected\_delivery\_date), train\_bookings(trip\_id), truck\_schedules(driver\_id), truck\_schedules(assistant\_id), truck\_schedules(start\_time, end\_time), deliveries(order\_id), order\_items(order\_id), train\_trips(destination\_city, departure\_date).  
* Additional indexes should be added wherever query analysis shows table scans on large tables.

## **6.2 Stored Procedures Required**

| Procedure Name | Purpose | Key Validations Inside |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| place\_order() | Creates order, books train space, assigns route | 7-day rule, route coverage, capacity check, overflow to next trip |
| schedule\_truck\_delivery() | Creates a truck schedule | Overlap check, consecutive driver rule, assistant rule, weekly hours |
| receive\_goods\_at\_store() | Records goods received from a train trip | Increments store inventory per product |
| complete\_delivery() | Marks delivery done, updates order status | Validates delivery exists, triggers status update |

## **6.3 Functions Required**

| Function Name | Returns | Used By |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| calculate\_order\_space(order\_id) | DECIMAL – total space units | place\_order(), capacity check trigger |
| get\_available\_capacity(trip\_id) | DECIMAL – remaining space | place\_order(), UI display |
| get\_driver\_weekly\_hours(driver\_id, week\_start) | DECIMAL – total hours | schedule\_truck\_delivery(), Report 4 |
| get\_assistant\_weekly\_hours(assistant\_id, week\_start) | DECIMAL – total hours | schedule\_truck\_delivery(), Report 4 |
| get\_next\_available\_trip(city, after\_date) | INT – trip\_id | place\_order() overflow logic |

## **6.4 Triggers Required**

| Trigger Name | Event | Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| trg\_validate\_order\_date | BEFORE INSERT on orders | Raise error if expected\_delivery\_date \< order\_date \+ 7 days |
| trg\_check\_trip\_capacity | BEFORE INSERT on train\_bookings | Raise error if booked space would exceed trip capacity |
| trg\_update\_trip\_booked\_space | AFTER INSERT on train\_bookings | Update running booked\_space total on train\_trips |
| trg\_validate\_truck\_schedule | BEFORE INSERT on truck\_schedules | Check overlap and roster rules for truck, driver, assistant |
| trg\_delivery\_complete\_order | AFTER UPDATE on deliveries | When status \= Completed, set linked order status \= Delivered |

## **6.5 Minimum Test Data Requirements**

* Products: Minimum 10 different FMCG products, each with name, category, unit price (LKR), and space consumption rate\[Subject to Change\].  
* Customers: Minimum 20 customers distributed across all six destination cities\[Subject to Change\].  
* Train Schedule: Valid schedule covering all six cities with defined capacities. Minimum 2 trips per city.  
* Routes: Minimum 10 delivery routes with at least one per city.  
* Drivers and Assistants: Minimum 8 drivers and 8 assistants\[Subject to Change\].   
* Trucks: Minimum 6 trucks\[Subject to Change\].  
* Orders: Minimum 40 orders distributed across different customers, cities, products, and time periods covering at least two quarters.  
* Truck Schedules and Deliveries: Sufficient records to demonstrate completed deliveries, including at least 5 pending deliveries for testing\[Subject to Change\].

# **Appendix A: Glossary**

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| ACID | Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability – the four properties of reliable database transactions. |
| Cargo Capacity | The maximum number of space units a single train trip can carry, defined per trip. |
| Consecutive Delivery | For drivers, a second truck schedule whose start time falls within 2 hours of the end of the immediately preceding schedule for the same driver. |
| Driver | An employee authorised to operate a delivery truck for last-mile customer deliveries. |
| Driver Assistant | An employee who accompanies the driver on delivery runs to assist with unloading. |
| FMCG | Fast-Moving Consumer Goods – products that are sold quickly and at relatively low cost, such as detergent, food, and beverages. |
| Last-Mile Delivery | The final stage of delivery from a city store to the customer's address, performed by road truck. |
| Order | A customer request to purchase one or more products for delivery to a specified address. |
| Order Item | A single product-quantity line within an order. |
| Overflow | The situation where an order's cargo space requirement exceeds the remaining capacity on an assigned train trip, causing part of the order to be moved to the next available trip. |
| Route | A predefined delivery path from a city store to a set of customer delivery zones, with a fixed maximum delivery time. |
| Space Consumption Rate | The number of train cargo space units consumed by one unit of a specific product (e.g., 0.5 units per box of detergent). |
| Space Unit | The standard unit of cargo space measurement, equivalent to the space occupied by one standard 50kg sack of rice. |
| Store | A warehouse or storage facility located near a railway station in a destination city, where goods are held between train arrival and truck dispatch. |
| Train Trip | One scheduled rail journey from Kandy to a destination city, with a fixed cargo capacity and departure/arrival times. |
| Train Booking | The record of cargo space reserved on a train trip for a specific order or set of order items. |
| Truck Schedule | An assignment of a truck, driver, and assistant to a specific delivery route on a specific date and time. |
| Weekly Limit | The maximum total hours a driver (40 hours) or assistant (60 hours) may be scheduled per calendar week. |
